1.why: Four different transition families with no duplicate; 'For instance' is the illustration slot these sets usually key to.

2.why: Three bare connectors against one elaborated hedge, 'In some circumstances, however,' - the specific option is the odd one out.

3.why: Restatement/contrast/similarity are all one-word stock distractors; 'For instance' is the only exemplifying option.

4.why: Only C states a method ('compared satellite images ... measuring the horizontal distance'); the others give cause, result, or motive.

5.why: Only B contains both halves of the contrast ('Doctors once blamed ... but Marshall and Warren showed').

6.why: Only C generalizes beyond the two cities ('a 2021 review of 40 cities'), which is what 'skeptical reader' demands.

7.why: Restatement, cause and correspondence cluster together; 'Even so' is the lone concessive.

8.why: Contrast, comparison and reason are hedge-shaped distractors; 'As a result' is the plain consequence slot.

9.why: Four options identical except for numbers (days lit, service interval); nothing in the set distinguishes them - pure guess.

10.why: 'For this reason' and 'Thus' are near-synonyms so neither can be the key; between the remaining two I take the contrast.

11.why: Cause, similarity and qualification against one exemplifier; 'For instance' is the distinct function.

12.why: Four templated clones differing only in cultivar name and held variable; 'Salinas' is the commonest research lettuce - effectively a guess.

13.why: Similarity, restatement and result are the stock trio; 'Nevertheless' is the only concessive.

14.why: Only C both names the principle and supplies the example ('though separated by over 400 million years, both independently evolved').

15.why: Only A puts both numbers side by side ('up to 3,000 miles ... as far as 9,000 miles'); B and C give one species each.

16.why: Only A spans decline and return ('closed ... in 1980, a cleanup restored it and swimmers returned in 2018').

17.why: Consequence, addition and restatement are the filler trio; 'However' is the only contrastive.

18.why: Only C strings the whole chain ('otters hold urchin numbers down and let kelp thrive, so kelp collapsed ... and rebounded').

19.why: Only A rebuts ('Far from vanishing ... rebounded to about 540,000'); B, C and D all report decline.

20.why: Four clones differing only in fouling organism and thickness; blue mussels are the usual dominant by weight - a guess.

21.why: Four clones differing only in the caveat; B's 'no unlit path used for comparison' is the limitation that most defeats the causal claim.

22.why: Only A links the steps ('wolves returned ... elk avoided the open valleys, allowing the willow and aspen ... to regrow').

23.why: Only A names one driver of several effects ('Rising ocean temperatures drove several changes at once').

24.why: Consequence, similarity and restatement are the stock trio; 'That said' is the lone concessive.
